taxonomy.subtopic: Colonic secretion after loss of apical sodium-dependent bile acid transport

questions.stem_html: A 34-year-old woman undergoes resection of diseased terminal ileum for Crohn disease. Several weeks later, she develops frequent watery stools that are most severe after meals. Stool cultures are negative, and there is no blood in the stool. The accompanying enterohepatic-circulation diagram shows reduced return of bile acids to the liver. Which mechanism most directly causes her diarrhea?

options.text_html: Reduced gastrin release prevents adequate gastric acid secretion and protein digestion
Increased ileal fibroblast growth factor 19 suppresses hepatic bile acid synthesis
Failure of pancreatic lipase secretion leaves osmotically active triglycerides in the small bowel
Unabsorbed bile acids reach the colon and stimulate electrolyte secretion and motility
Loss of jejunal lactase causes fermentation of dietary lactose after every meal

questions.explanation_html: Most bile acids are actively reclaimed in the terminal ileum through the apical sodium-dependent bile acid transporter. Ileal inflammation or resection interrupts this process. Excess bile acids then enter the colon, where they promote water and electrolyte secretion and increase motility, producing bile acid diarrhea. Reduced ileal bile acid signaling also lowers fibroblast growth factor 19 feedback and can increase hepatic bile acid synthesis, which may further enlarge the colonic bile acid load.

wrong_choice_explanations.2: Pancreatic enzyme deficiency causes fat maldigestion and steatorrhea but is not the primary consequence of terminal ileal resection.
wrong_choice_explanations.3: Lactase deficiency causes carbohydrate-related osmotic diarrhea and would depend on lactose exposure rather than terminal ileal loss.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: Gastrin and gastric acid secretion are not primarily controlled by the terminal ileum.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: Terminal ileal bile acid loss decreases, rather than increases, fibroblast growth factor 19 feedback to the liver.

questions.educational_objective: Terminal ileal disease or resection prevents bile acid reclamation; bile acids entering the colon stimulate secretion and motility, causing watery diarrhea.
